expectations.text: Quotes or paraphrases the desire contract idea
expectations.evidence: Quotes exactly: "Desire is a contract you make with yourself to be unhappy until you get what you want." (matches SKILL.md).
"Seek wealth, not money or status." with definitions: wealth = assets that earn while you sleep, money = how we transfer time and wealth, status = place in the social hierarchy (all match SKILL.md).

expectations.text: Explains one-desire-at-a-time or choosing desires carefully
expectations.evidence: Thread 1: 'His advice is to choose your desires carefully and keep them few, ideally one at a time'; frames wealth as 'one deliberately chosen desire'. Matches SKILL.md 'Pick desires carefully, one at a time'.

expectations.text: Explains wealth as freedom/means to stop playing games
expectations.evidence: Thread 3: wealth is worth seeking because it 'solves money problems and buys back your time and freedom: freedom from having to rent out your hours'; Thread 2 contrasts positive-sum wealth with zero-sum status games; Thread 5 uses the retirement quote (matches SKILL.md).

expectations.text: Mentions peace/happiness being separate from success
expectations.evidence: 'The book insists that success does not earn happiness'; happiness as 'the state when nothing is missing, with peace as happiness at rest'; table separating Wealth (Part I) from Happiness (Part II). All match SKILL.md.
